case_file.environment: Node 22+, tsconfig strict, bun test, Windows + bash
case_file.observation: Boot orphan-cleanup removes chain files in three cases (state-belongs-to-chain-completed, state-belongs-to-chain-cleared-mid, state-terminal-with-no-chainId). The guard `bootTerminalState` (line 1087) is set ONLY when readGoalStateResult returns kind === 'ok' AND the state is achieved or cleared. If the state file is absent or corrupt, bootTerminalState is null and the entire chain cleanup block is skipped — a chain file with no corresponding state file lingers forever.
case_file.expected_invariant: On boot, an orphan chain file (chain file present, state file absent or non-terminal-or-orphaning) MUST be unlinked. The chain should not survive a session where the goal that owned it no longer exists in any recoverable form.
case_file.audited_claim: C0: The boot orphan-cleanup logic at packages/autogoal/src/server.ts:1075-1111 has a fourth orphan case not handled — chain file exists AND state file is absent or corrupt. The block guards on `bootTerminalState` truthy (line 1087), which is null when readGoalStateResult returns kind === 'absent' or kind === 'corrupt'. This is the most-orphaned a chain can be (no goal to bind to), and it is missed by the recent fix in commit 6d7d0c049.
case_file.center_anchor: packages/autogoal/src/server.ts:1075-1111 [chain cleanup block] paired with packages/autogoal/src/server.ts:1047 [bootTerminalState declaration] and packages/autogoal/src/goal-state.ts:656 [readGoalStateResult signature]
case_file.falsifier: Reproduce: in a fresh tmp directory, write a valid chain file via writeGoalChain, then leave the state file absent (or write a syntactically corrupt state file). Boot the plugin. Observe whether the chain file is unlinked. If it IS unlinked, C0 fails.

fusion.root_cause: The cleanup block at server.ts:1087 uses `if (c.kind === "ok" && c.value.steps.length > 0 && bootTerminalState)` — three conjunctive conditions. The `bootTerminalState` guard excludes the absent-or-corrupt state case. There is no separate code path that handles 'chain exists but no recoverable state.' The intent of the recent fix (commit 6d7d0c049) was to broaden orphan detection; it broadened the terminal-state cases but not the missing-state case.
fusion.terminal_impact: A user who clears the chain file's owning state file (or whose state file becomes corrupt) will see the chain file linger across boots. The next chain operation will pick it up as a stale chain (chainMatchesGoal in goal-panel-pure.ts:128 will reject it because the new state has no chainId, but the file remains on disk). Repeated occurrences grow the .opencode/ directory with stale artifacts; manual cleanup is the only remediation. The contract test at goal-panel-contract.test.ts:206-210 already pins the chainMatchesGoal semantics, so the UI does not misrender — but the file system state drifts.

evidence.method: Focused read of the cleanup block after the recent fix. The block is guarded by `if (c.kind === "ok" && c.value.steps.length > 0 && bootTerminalState)`. The `bootTerminalState` value is null whenever readGoalStateResult returns anything other than kind === 'ok' with status in {achieved, cleared}.
evidence.result: Three-orphan-cases block does NOT execute when state file is absent or corrupt. The chain cleanup is silently skipped.

evidence.method: Focused read of bootTerminalState assignment. The variable is declared `let bootTerminalState: GoalState | null = null;` and is only set inside the `if (r.kind === "ok" && (r.value.status === "achieved" || r.value.status === "cleared"))` branch. Three pre-existing failures of this guard exist: read returns kind === 'absent', kind === 'corrupt', or kind === 'ok' but with status 'active' or 'paused'.
evidence.result: bootTerminalState is null in three pre-existing-failure cases; two of them (absent, corrupt) are orphan-chain territory not addressed by the recent fix.

evidence.method: Focused read. readGoalStateResult returns ReadResult<GoalState> which is a discriminated union of kind: 'ok' | 'corrupt' (and conceptually 'absent'). When kind !== 'ok', bootTerminalState is not assigned.
evidence.result: readGoalStateResult's three non-ok return kinds all leave bootTerminalState null. The cleanup block then skips orphan detection.

confirmed_defects.claim: The boot orphan-cleanup does not unlink chain files when the state file is absent or corrupt. Such chains linger forever across boots.
confirmed_defects.root_cause: The cleanup block guards on `bootTerminalState` truthy (line 1087). This value is null when the state file is absent, corrupt, or in a non-terminal state. There is no separate code path that handles 'chain exists but state is unrecoverable.' The recent fix (6d7d0c049) broadened terminal-state coverage but did not address the missing-state case.
confirmed_defects.impact: Users who clear their state file (manually or via a bug) or whose state file becomes corrupt will accumulate stale chain files in .opencode/. The files do not misrender the UI (chainMatchesGoal rejects them) but they consume disk and require manual cleanup. Repeated occurrences grow the .opencode/ directory indefinitely.

disproven_concerns.concern: Could the guard have been intentionally omitted to preserve chains during the 'active' or 'paused' state, and is the missing-state case actually an orphan?
disproven_concerns.evidence_of_absence: A chain file with no state file CANNOT be associated with an active or paused goal — there is no state to bind to. The 'active/paused preserves the chain' invariant applies only when state is recoverable (readGoalStateResult returns ok). When state is absent or corrupt, there is no recoverable goal-state binding the chain; the chain is by definition orphaned.
disproven_concerns.scope_limits: The disproof is bounded to 'chain file present + state file absent or corrupt.' It does not cover the case where the chain file itself is corrupt (readGoalChainResult returns kind === 'corrupt'); that case is a separate concern beyond this audit's center.

unknowns.description: What is the actual rate at which users encounter missing-state conditions? Manual state-file deletion is rare but not impossible; state-file corruption via partial writes has a known prior (see line 1044-1046 comment about 'previous code unlinked first, then re-read the now-absent file — so the chain was never cleaned up'). The frequency would inform whether this is MEDIUM (occasional) or LOW (rare).
unknowns.evidence_needed: Production telemetry on state-file corruption frequency over the last 90 days, plus manual user reports of stale chain files.
unknowns.confidence_effect: Does not change CERTAIN likelihood or HIGH confidence; only refines impact between MEDIUM and LOW.

non_center_observations.observation: The unlinkSync call is wrapped in try/catch and logs at debug level on failure. A failed unlink (e.g., permission error) would leave the chain file in place silently. This is a separate concern from C0.
non_center_observations.exclusion_reason: Out of scope: C0 is about whether the cleanup runs at all when state is missing. The unlink-failure-silent path is a different failure mode (cleanup runs but unlink fails silently). Flagged for follow-up.

non_center_observations.observation: The function at goal-state.ts:1109 returns null if state is not active or paused. This is correctly handling the terminal case at the read-state API level. The boot-cleanup block could conceivably use this helper instead of readGoalStateResult + manual status check, which would simplify the bootTerminalState guard.
non_center_observations.exclusion_reason: Out of scope: refactor opportunity, not a defect. C0 is a behavior defect (missing case), not a code-structure defect.

repair_contract.objective: Broaden the boot orphan-cleanup guard so a chain file is unlinked when the state file is absent or corrupt, in addition to the three existing terminal-state cases.
repair_contract.required_invariant: On boot, a chain file present in .opencode/ is unlinked if EITHER (a) the state file shows the goal as terminal and the chain belongs to that state or no state, OR (b) the state file is absent, OR (c) the state file is corrupt (cannot be read). The only case where the chain file MUST be preserved is when state is active or paused and the chain belongs to it.

compatibility: Active/paused goals must continue to preserve their chain file across boots (the existing invariant).
The three terminal-state cases fixed in commit 6d7d0c049 must continue to be handled.

repair_contract.reversibility: Single-function edit (the guard logic at server.ts:1087) + one new test file. Revert by git revert of the fix commit. The original three-case behavior is preserved by the existing tests; only the missing/corrupt case is added.
